Day 5, evening. After supper, [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] asked his parents if he could climb the hill again soon, with the same rule — home before dark. His father said yes, the rule holds. Rosa arrived at the gate, having waited through supper to work up the nerve; she asked to come next time, and [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] said yes.

He then remembered the wooden treehouse observatory is half Marcos's, and asked aloud whether he could show it to Elena. Marcos tapped his walking stick twice — his sign that a true answer is coming — and said, simply, "Show her."

Together, [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] and Marcos climbed the ladder into the treehouse. On the high shelf where the evening light fell longest, [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] placed Captain Crunch and arranged the forty-three smooth stones around it. Below, through the open door, Bruno circled three times and settled into the dust, at ease. The first true stars came out. Marcos stood beside him without speaking, one hand on a support beam, his walking stick left on the ground. [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] said, "Next time, we will show her this." Marcos nodded.

Nothing is open. The hill has been crossed and will be crossed again, with Rosa next time and Elena welcome at the observatory. Captain Crunch and the stones now sit together on the high shelf. The book ends on the two of them under the opening sky.
